questions.q: What does "Configure > Form Layout" actually do?
options: Moves fields between the form and an available-fields list, and reorders them — it doesn't create or delete fields
Creates a brand-new field in the table's dictionary
Deletes the underlying dictionary entry for a field
Changes the table's database engine
questions.explain: Form Layout is a view-level operation. The field's definition in sys_dictionary is untouched; only what this form displays changes.

questions.q: Why do forms get broken into sections?
options: Pure usability — grouping related fields so a user isn't shown every field at once
Because ServiceNow requires exactly one section per table
Sections are a database-level partitioning mechanism
Sections replace the need for list views entirely
questions.explain: Sections (often shown as tabs) group fields like closure information so they're easy to collapse until actually needed.

questions.q: What problem does a UI Policy solve that a permanent Form Layout change can't?
options: Conditional behavior — showing, hiding, or requiring fields based on live values as the user fills out the form
Permanently deleting a field from the table
Changing which users can log in to the instance
Sorting a list view's columns
questions.explain: UI Policies react live to form conditions (e.g., Category = Hardware), unlike a static Form Layout change that applies unconditionally.

questions.q: If you remove a field from an Incident form using Form Layout, what happens to that field's data on existing records?
options: Nothing — the data and the dictionary entry are untouched; only this form stops displaying the field
The data is permanently deleted from every incident record
The field is renamed automatically
All other forms on the table also stop showing the field
questions.explain: Form Layout only changes what one form displays. Other forms, reports, and list views built on the same table are unaffected.

questions.q: Where do you configure UI Policies at the basic, no-scripting level?
options: System UI > UI Policies
System Definition > Tables
The user's own profile/preferences menu
System Properties, instance-wide only
questions.explain: System UI > UI Policies is the module for configuring basic conditional field behavior without writing script.
